question: Will DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth-memory contract prices stay elevated (or keep rising) through calendar 2026, keeping memory at roughly 25–30% of an NVIDIA AI rack's bill of materials and a potential constraint on AI-system build volumes?
outcome: Direction and level of DRAM/NAND/HBM contract pricing during calendar 2026 and whether memory supply stays tight enough to constrain NVIDIA's Vera Rubin rack build volumes.
period: Calendar 2026 — memory contract pricing for this calendar year; the item gives no release date, so the period is fixed by the reason (a shared price several companies depend on for this year) and settled by memory price trackers and memory makers' quarterly reports.

question: What will contract prices for the memory going into NVIDIA's racks (DRAM/LPDDR5X, 3D NAND, HBM) average over calendar 2027, and how much memory cost per Vera Rubin VR200 NVL72 rack will that imply versus the ~$2 million per rack Morgan Stanley estimates for the first shipments?
outcome: The average contract price of DRAM/LPDDR5X/NAND (and HBM) bought for NVIDIA AI racks in calendar 2027 and the resulting memory content per VR200 rack, measured against the ~$2 million per rack / 25-30% of bill of materials Morgan Stanley estimates now.
period: Calendar 2027 average contract prices, checked at the memory contract-price survey releases through 2027 — set by the reason (a shared input price outside any one company); the item gives no specific release date, so the check is the 2027 series of contract-price releases.

question: How much will memory (DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory) contract prices rise over calendar 2026–2027, pushing up the memory cost embedded in AI infrastructure and devices that NVIDIA and its customers depend on?
outcome: The change in DRAM/NAND/HBM contract prices and the resulting memory-content cost per AI rack over calendar 2026–2027.
period: Calendar 2026–2027 (the item's 'second half of 2026 and beyond').
